title: Inversion (2)
summary: Инверсия в условных без **if** (**Should / Were / Had**), после **so / such**, в ответах **so / neither / nor** и с наречиями места (**Here comes..., In the corner stood...**).
ru:
## Условные предложения без if
В формальной речи и письме **if** можно опустить, если сделать инверсию: вспомогательный глагол выходит вперёд, как в вопросе.
- **Should** + подлежащее + инфинитив — «если вдруг» (реальное или маловероятное условие): *If you need help, call us.* → **Should you need** help, call us. — Если вам понадобится помощь, позвоните нам.
- **Were** + подлежащее (+ to + инфинитив) — нереальное настоящее / будущее: *If I were in your position...* → **Were I** in your position, I would accept. — *If she resigned...* → **Were she to resign**, the company would collapse.
- **Had** + подлежащее + причастие — нереальное прошлое: *If we had known...* → **Had we known** about the delay, we would have taken another flight.
Отрицание: **не сливается** с вспомогательным глаголом — *Had I not been so tired*, но не ~~Hadn't I been~~. Аналогично: **Were it not for** your help... / **Had it not been for** the rescuers... — «если бы не...».

## so и such в начале предложения
Для эффекта вперёд выносят группу с **so + прилагательное** или **such + be**; после этой группы — инверсия.
> **So fierce was** the storm that all flights were cancelled. — Шторм был таким сильным, что отменили все рейсы.
> **Such was** the demand for tickets that the website crashed. — Спрос на билеты был так велик, что сайт «упал».
Это литературный и формальный приём; в разговорной речи скажут *The storm was so fierce that...*

## so, neither, nor: согласие
Чтобы сказать «я тоже», используют **so** (в утверждениях) и **neither / nor** (в отрицаниях) + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее. Вспомогательный повторяет время и форму исходной фразы.
> 'I'm exhausted.' — '**So am I.**' — Я тоже.
> 'I haven't seen it.' — '**Neither have I.**' / '**Nor have I.**' — Я тоже не видел.
> She can't swim, and **nor can** her sister. — Она не умеет плавать, и её сестра тоже.
Если нужно просто подтвердить (не «тоже»), инверсии нет: *'You said it would rain.' — 'So it did.'* — То есть «и правда, так и было».

## Наречия места и направления
В описаниях и повествовании наречие места или направления выносят в начало, а глагол ставят перед подлежащим. Так бывает с глаголами положения и движения (**be, stand, lie, sit, come, go, hang**) и обычно с подлежащим-существительным.
> **Here comes** the bus! — А вот и автобус!
> **In the corner stood** an old piano. — В углу стояло старое пианино.
> **Down came** the rain. — Хлынул дождь.
> **On the wall hung** a huge mirror. — На стене висело огромное зеркало.
Но если подлежащее — **местоимение**, инверсии нет: ***Here it comes!*** / ***Away he ran.*** (не ~~Here comes it~~).

## Другие случаи
- **than / as** в формальных текстах: *She earns more than does her brother.* — *He was late, as were the others.*
- Слова автора после прямой речи: *'Come in,' said the teacher.* — (но с местоимением обычно *she said*).
- Устойчивые формулы: **Long live** the Queen! · **May** you be happy! · **Be that as it may** · **Gone are the days** when...

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~Should you will need help, call us.~~ → **Should you need** help, call us.
- ~~Hadn't we known...~~ → Had we **not** known...
- ~~So loud the music was that...~~ → So loud **was the music** that...
- ~~Here comes it.~~ → Here **it comes**.
- ~~Neither I have seen it.~~ → Neither **have I** seen it.
en:
## Conditional sentences without if
In formal speech and writing we can leave out **if** and use inversion: the auxiliary verb goes in front of the subject, as in a question.
- **Should** + subject + infinitive — "in case" (a real or unlikely condition): *If you need help, call us.* → **Should you need** help, call us.
- **Were** + subject (+ to + infinitive) — unreal present or future: *If I were in your position...* → **Were I** in your position, I would accept. — *If she resigned...* → **Were she to resign**, the company would collapse.
- **Had** + subject + past participle — unreal past: *If we had known...* → **Had we known** about the delay, we would have taken another flight.
In the negative, **not does not contract** with the auxiliary: *Had I not been so tired*, never ~~Hadn't I been~~. Similar structures: **Were it not for** your help... / **Had it not been for** the rescuers... meaning "if it hadn't been for...".

## so and such at the start of a sentence
For effect, we can put a phrase with **so + adjective** or **such + be** at the front. Inversion follows.
> **So fierce was** the storm that all flights were cancelled.
> **Such was** the demand for tickets that the website crashed.
This is a literary and formal device; in conversation people say *The storm was so fierce that...*

## so, neither, nor: agreeing
To say "me too", we use **so** (after positive statements) and **neither / nor** (after negative ones) + auxiliary + subject. The auxiliary repeats the tense and form of the original sentence.
> 'I'm exhausted.' — '**So am I.**'
> 'I haven't seen it.' — '**Neither have I.**' / '**Nor have I.**'
> She can't swim, and **nor can** her sister.
If we only confirm what was said (not "also"), there is no inversion: *'You said it would rain.' — 'So it did.'* meaning "yes, that is what happened".

## Adverbs of place and direction
In descriptions and narrative, an adverbial of place or direction can go first, with the verb before the subject. This happens with verbs of position and movement (**be, stand, lie, sit, come, go, hang**), usually with a noun subject.
> **Here comes** the bus!
> **In the corner stood** an old piano.
> **Down came** the rain.
> **On the wall hung** a huge mirror.
But if the subject is a **pronoun**, there is no inversion: ***Here it comes!*** / ***Away he ran.*** (not ~~Here comes it~~).

## Other cases
- **than / as** in formal texts: *She earns more than does her brother.* — *He was late, as were the others.*
- Reporting words after direct speech: *'Come in,' said the teacher.* (with a pronoun we usually say *she said*).
- Fixed expressions: **Long live** the Queen! · **May** you be happy! · **Be that as it may** · **Gone are the days** when...

## Common mistakes
- ~~Should you will need help, call us.~~ → **Should you need** help, call us.
- ~~Hadn't we known...~~ → Had we **not** known...
- ~~So loud the music was that...~~ → So loud **was the music** that...
- ~~Here comes it.~~ → Here **it comes**.
- ~~Neither I have seen it.~~ → Neither **have I** seen it.
structure:
## Условные без if
| Тип | Формула | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Should (вдруг) | Should + S + V | Should you need help, call me. |
| Were (нереальное настоящее) | Were + S (+ to V) | Were I you, I'd wait. |
| Had (нереальное прошлое) | Had + S + V3 | Had we known, we would have left. |
| Если бы не | Were it not for / Had it not been for | Had it not been for him, we'd have failed. |

## so / such / место
| Модель | Пример |
|---|---|
| So + adj + be / aux + S + that | So heavy was the rain that the roads flooded. |
| Such + be + NP + that | Such was her anger that she left. |
| Here / There + V + noun | Here comes the bus. |
| Place + V + noun | In the doorway stood a tall man. |
| Pronoun subject: без инверсии | Here it comes. · Away he went. |

## so / neither / nor
| Исходная фраза | Ответ |
|---|---|
| I'm tired. | So am I. |
| I've finished. | So have I. |
| I don't know. | Neither do I. / Nor do I. |
| She can't come. | Nor can he. |
| (подтверждение) You said it would rain. | So it did. (инверсии нет) |

exercises.title: Вставьте нужное слово
exercises.instruction: Вставьте недостающее слово. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: {{Should}} you need any further information, please contact our office.
{{Were}} I in your position, I would accept the offer.
{{Had}} we known about the delay, we would have taken another flight.
So fierce {{was}} the storm that all flights were cancelled.
Such {{was}} the demand for tickets that the website crashed.
I don't like fish, and neither {{does}} my brother.
She can't swim, and nor {{can}} her sister.
In the corner of the room {{stood}} an old piano.
{{Were}} it not for your help, we would have failed.
{{Had}} it not been for the rescuers, the climbers would have died.
She earns far more than {{does}} her husband.
You told me it would rain, and so {{it}} did.

items.q: ___ you require assistance, please ask at the desk. (без if)
items.why: **Should you require** — формальное условие без if.

items.q: ___ I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
So heavy ___ that the bridge collapsed.
items.why: После **So + adj** — **was the snowfall** (be без do).

items.q: Such ___ that nobody dared to speak.
Behind the door ___ a tall stranger.
items.why: Место + глагол положения + подлежащее: **stood a tall stranger**.

options: Were she to resign, the company would collapse.
Was she to resign, the company would collapse.
If were she to resign, the company would collapse.
items.why: **Were she to** + инфинитив; Was в такой инверсии не используется.

options: Had I not been so tired, I would have joined you.
Had I been not so tired, I would have joined you.
Did I not been so tired, I would have joined you.
items.why: Отрицание ставится после подлежащего: **Had I not been**.

options: I can't stand noise, and neither can my neighbour.
I can't stand noise, and neither my neighbour can.
I can't stand noise, and neither does can my neighbour.
On the wall hung a huge mirror.
On the wall a huge mirror did hang.
items.why: Место + глагол + существительное: **hung a huge mirror**.
С местоимением инверсии нет: **Away he ran**.

options: So tired was she that she fell asleep at once.
So tired she was that she fell asleep at once.
So tired did she that she fell asleep at once.
Nor have I ever regretted it.
Nor I have ever regretted it.
Nor have ever I regretted it.

exercises.title: Перепишите без if / с инверсией
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, начав с указанного слова.

items.prompt: Start with **Should**: If you need a refund, contact us immediately.
answers: Should you need a refund, contact us immediately.

items.prompt: Start with **Were**: If I were you, I wouldn't sign it.
answers: Were I you, I wouldn't sign it.
Were I you, I would not sign it.

items.prompt: Start with **Had**: If we hadn't missed the bus, we would have arrived on time.
answers: Had we not missed the bus, we would have arrived on time.

items.prompt: Start with **So**: The noise was so loud that nobody could sleep.
answers: So loud was the noise that nobody could sleep.

items.prompt: Start with **Such**: His disappointment was so great that he left the room.
answers: Such was his disappointment that he left the room.

items.prompt: Agree with 'I haven't seen the report yet.' using **neither** or **nor**.
Start with **Were it not for**: If it weren't for your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.
answers: Were it not for your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.

items.prompt: Start with **In the doorway**: A tall man stood in the doorway.
answers: In the doorway stood a tall man.

items.prompt: Start with **Here**: The bus is coming!
Start with **Down**: The rain came down.
Reply with **so**: 'I was really impressed by the lecture.' (you too)
Start with **Should anyone**: If anyone calls, say that I'm out.
answers: Should anyone call, say that I'm out.
Should anyone call, say I'm out.
Should anyone call, tell them that I'm out.
Should anyone call, tell them I'm out.

items.prompt: Write a formal sentence starting with **Should you**: what would you tell a visitor to your city?
items.sample: Should you visit my city, I recommend the old market.

items.prompt: Write a sentence about a past regret. Start with **Had I**.
items.sample: Had I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

items.prompt: Write about a time when something was extremely loud, cold or expensive. Start with **So**.
items.sample: So loud was the concert that my ears were ringing for hours.

items.prompt: Agree with a statement of your own choice using **so** or **neither**. Write both the statement and your answer.
Describe a room you know well. Start with **In the corner stood** or **On the wall hung**.
items.sample: In the corner of my room stood an old wooden desk.
